skills.description: Through fixed aquarium cameras, the system analyzes fish behavior near the water surface, detecting repeated mouth-out-of-water (gasping), rapid mouth opening/closing (fast respiration) and exaggerated operculum (gill cover) movement — classic symptoms of hypoxia or poisoning. When multiple fish exhibit the above behavior simultaneously and the duration exceeds a configurable threshold (default 60 seconds), the system outputs an 'ammonia poisoning or hypoxia risk warning', prompting the user to immediately test water quality, perform water change, or increase aeration. This skill helps take emergency action BEFORE fish die. Application scenarios: home aquariums, public aquariums, aquaculture ponds. The system monitors in real time and pushes alerts the moment fish gasping is detected. Skill features: ammonia poisoning is a common acute emergency in aquariums — by the time it is noticed, fish deaths may have already occurred.
